concept.name: Trading volume
concept.definition: Trading volume is the total number of units of a security (shares, contracts, or coins) that changed hands in executed trades during a given period. It is the standard measure of market activity and is reported per instrument, per venue, or consolidated across venues.
concept.intuition: Volume counts how much of an asset actually traded. It tells you how active and liquid the market was, not which direction prices moved.
concept.mechanics: Each executed trade contributes its quantity to the period total; volume is typically aggregated per bar (e.g., daily) and reported alongside OHLC prices. Average volume over a longer window is total volume divided by the number of periods.
concept.formula: V = Σ_i q_i, where q_i is the quantity of trade i executed during the period. Average volume = Σ V_t / N over N periods.
concept.failure_modes: Volume can be inflated by wash trading (especially on unregulated crypto venues) and understated when off-exchange or dark-pool prints are excluded from a feed. Raw volume says nothing about direction, so a high-volume day can coincide with either a rally or a crash.
concept.misconceptions: High volume does not mean the price rose or will rise — it only means many units changed hands. Comparing share volume across stocks of different prices is meaningless without converting to dollar volume.
concept.example: If 2.1 million shares of AAPL trade on a given day, that day's volume is 2.1 million shares; if the 30-day average is 55 million shares, the day was unusually quiet.
